children: *Lucky Strike CEO Thomas Shannon Offers to Buy Company for $4.35/Shr
*Lucky Strike CEO Believes Share Price Has Been Hurt by 'Market Conditions Affecting Current Investors' Attitude About Site-Based Businesses Generally'
Lucky Strike Shares Rise on CEO Buyout Proposal
Lucky Strike Entertainment shares were higher after Chief Executive Thomas Shannon proposed a buyout for $4.35 a share.
The stock was recently up 22% to $4.05 and is down about 52% this year.
The company's operations include Lucky Strike, Bowlero and AMF bowling chains, amusement parks and water parks.

Shannon noted that the share price has generally declined in recent years. "In my view, this has primarily been the result of market conditions affecting current investors' attitude about site-based businesses generally," he said.

Shannon said a buyout would provide a premium to stockholders and "provide a better context in which to reposition our business for the long term while saving the out-of-pocket costs and distraction of remaining publicly traded."
